clue.text: National articles (including a series of letters)

indicators.note: including means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
AN is the other form of the indefinite article
F, G, H is a run of consecutive letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A grammar point about a country's articles, with a sequence of letters slipped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here: a citizen of a country, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Afghanistan is called by this nationality word, so a national of that country fits.

clue.text: What's better than a full house as cause for reform?

definitions.text: What's better than a full house

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poker question dressed up as a political reason for reforming something.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, four of a kind beats a full house (three of a kind plus a pair).
explanation.definitionFit: A hand of four of a kind outranks a full house in standard poker hand rankings.

clue.text: Keeps register to put a stop to motion

parts.note: to keep something is to hold it, giving holds
a cash register is a till

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a record in order to halt a proposal at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'register' and 'motion' suggest record-keeping and a formal proposal; here they are a cash till and physical movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying perfectly motionless is the idiom, meaning to stop moving altogether.

clue.text: Fine point of Germanic etymology

indicators.note: of signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A subtle detail about where Germanic words come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle distinction or precise detail is a synonym for a fine point.

clue.text: Said to hitch up with the enemy of the sea

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and we enter what they sound like

parts.note: to get hitched is to marry
time is proverbially the enemy

explanation.surface: A sinister suggestion of joining forces with the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' applies to the whole phrase: marry time spoken aloud gives the answer. 'Time is the enemy' is a common saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything connected with the ocean or seafaring, so it means relating to the sea.

clue.text: Order to pen rap music part here

definitions.text: Order to pen rap music part here

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to write out a rapper's part on the proper sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: rearrange the letters, and also it is where you would write down a musical part.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled staff sheets are the stationery on which musicians write out scores and parts by hand.

clue.text: Roguish partner chasing roguish cars

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the other
roguish means behaving wildly, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A shady companion following some disreputable cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roguish' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the signal to rearrange CARS into RASC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being like a scamp or knave, mischievous and dishonest, is to be roguish.

clue.text: Ultimately slept with family member to be provocative

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A scandalous tale of sleeping with a relative in order to shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer or goad someone with insults is to act provocatively towards them.

clue.text: A communist uprising blocks proposal for temperance

indicators.note: something that blocks a passage sits within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a motion is a formal proposal at a meeting

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the words from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A political story of a communist revolt obstructing a call for sobriety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns A RED into DERA, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance means restraint and avoiding excess, which is the same as keeping things within limits.

clue.text: Bird has no energy to collect dole money for the landlord

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one piece takes the other inside
has no means a letter is missing from the bird

parts.note: the pelican is a large water bird
E is the physics symbol for energy
UB is short for unemployment benefit, British dole money

explanation.surface: A bird without energy gathering welfare payments on behalf of a pub owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes E, leaving PLICAN; dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the person who keeps a pub, its landlord, is traditionally called by this title.

clue.text: Read about redhead getting tough

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to study is to read
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: Study up on a ginger-haired person becoming hardened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like a ginger-haired person; it is the head (first letter) of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something robust and strongly built is tough, a close synonym.

clue.text: Good or bad, sits a plant

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: an industrial plant is a factory

explanation.surface: Whatever its quality, someone sits a plant down somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good or bad' reads as a contrast; 'Good' is the definition and 'bad' the signal to rearrange SITS A into SATIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable or adequate work is described as good enough, which is this adjective's sense.

clue.text: Hotel needs hand in development

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
to give someone a hand is to applaud, and an ovation is applause

explanation.surface: A hotel short of staff needing an extra worker for a new project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' looks like a worker; it is applause, as in 'give them a big hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A new idea or invention is a development, the sense of something newly devised.

clue.text: Not in favour of Ain't Misbehavin'

indicators.note: misbehaving letters are unruly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disapproving of the jazz standard Ain't Misbehavin'.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title 'Ain't Misbehavin'' splits into the fodder and its own anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is the preposition's meaning, the reverse of pro.

clue.text: Porter back in speed move

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: rate means speed

indicators.note: back means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter

explanation.surface: A railway porter returning in a hurry to shift things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' is not a luggage carrier but the composer Cole Porter; 'back' turns his first name into ELOC.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something or someone to a new place is to move it there.

clue.text: Perhaps bishop with cold mouth and nose first to catch dreaded disease

indicators.note: to catch something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside
first picks the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the dreaded lergy is a jokey British name for an unspecified illness, from The Goon Show

explanation.surface: A bishop with a cold whose mouth and nose are about to catch something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dreaded lurgy' (here spelt lergy) is a comic British name for any vague illness, from the radio show The Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is an example of a churchman, hence the 'Perhaps' flagging the example.

clue.text: Stinger capable of releasing poison? It's often nasty to begin with

definitions.text: Stinger capable of releasing poison? It's often nasty to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each word

parts.words: Stinger capable of releasing poison? It's often nasty

explanation.surface: A description of a venomous creature with a reputation for nastiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the first eight words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This arachnid has a venomous sting in its tail and is widely feared as nasty.

clue.text: The odds on awful scoop splashed out in the paper

indicators.note: splashed out suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged
the odds are the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper splashing an awful exclusive across the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'awful' are A, F, L; with SCOOP they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional large size of writing or printing paper.

clue.text: God of generosity

indicators.note: of signals letters taken from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A deity known for giving freely.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love is a god, so the name fits the definition.

clue.text: Vulgar criminal Blair indicted at last

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked and rearranged
at last points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper-style cry that the former prime minister has finally been charged.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, crude or bawdy humour is vulgar, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What makes Bunny buy into pretentious behaviour?

wordplay.reading: BUNNY dropping N + N gives BUY

parts.note: N stands for name, so losing the names (both Ns) turns the word Bunny into buy

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what drives someone nicknamed Bunny to shop in a showy way.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for name; dropping both from BUNNY leaves BUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually mentioning famous acquaintances to impress others is a classic form of showing off.

clue.text: Be good when 40, as they say

indicators.note: as they say means the letters are spoken aloud

parts.note: XL is 40 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cheerful saying that life gets better at forty.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine or do especially well is to be good at something.

clue.text: See 2
Not half kick, my chilli pickles

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of each word is used

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a chilli has quite a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'very much'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Korean dish is fermented, pickled vegetables, mainly cabbage, so it counts as pickles.

clue.text: Fast harmful drugs here

parts.note: pacy means fast, and harmful is read as harm-full: the word for fast filled with harm

explanation.surface: A warning about dangerous fast-acting drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harmful' is read as 'harm-full', so the word for fast (PACY) is filled with HARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop is where medicines are dispensed, so it is where drugs are found.

clue.text: A single ship? That's a joke

parts.note: a single is one
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that a lone ship is laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip delivered in one sentence is a short joke.

clue.text: European leader to disappear a hundred times

indicators.note: the leading Roman five is multiplied by a hundred to give five hundred

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear

explanation.surface: A leader told to make themselves scarce over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' points at the first letter, V (5 in Roman numerals); a hundred times 5 is 500, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Denmark is a European, so the nationality fits.
